title: Ukraine strikes Russian air bases in Operation Spiderweb
body:
On 1 June 2025, Ukraine carried out a coordinated drone attack on Russian military airfields, known as Operation Spiderweb. The Security Service of Ukraine, or SBU, made the principal damage claims. According to the UK Defence Journal, the targets were five airbases: Olenya, Dyagilevo, Ivanovo Severny, Belaya and Voskresensk. Reported targets included Tu-160 and Tu-95 bombers and an A-50 airborne early warning aircraft.

The SBU claimed that more than 40 Russian military aircraft were destroyed, including strategic bombers and airborne command platforms. Ukrainian officials estimated the damage at more than 2 billion dollars. Russian officials did not confirm these figures. The Russian Ministry of Defence had not issued a comprehensive statement, though regional authorities confirmed drone attacks in several oblasts, and the governor of Irkutsk acknowledged a strike near Belaya.

Ukrainian sources said planning took 18 months and was overseen by President Volodymyr Zelensky. Drones were smuggled into Russia in disguised wooden crates mounted on mobile truck platforms, and were launched when the container roofs were opened remotely. The article refers to dozens of drones. Ukrainian agents involved in staging the drones were reportedly exfiltrated before the launch. According to Axios, Ukrainian officials informed the US administration in advance.

The UK Defence Journal noted that its account relied on Ukrainian claims and unofficial reporting, because no Russian damage assessment or casualty figures had been released.
